thread_title: S. leucophylla var. alba clone A Baldwin Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla var. alba clone A Baldwin Co, AL

posts.body_html:
You can't always judge a leucophylla by its summer traps: the best show is typically in the fall, when they produce their largest, whitest traps!

well, thought I'd start photo-documenting this clone: it looks like a regular leucophylla in the pics below, but don't be fooled, this one can get very white under ideal conditions! It's one of those chameleon clones but hey, the summer traps look like a decent regular leucophylla.

Removing pollen isn’t really damaging the environment. There was once a thing that plants were for the benefit of all and the idea that we can no longer sustainably collect plants and seeds because some idiots decided to go hog wild and rip out a bunch of plants is stupid. I’m not for poaching, but I wouldn’t go on begging some pea brained landowner to change his mind if he doesn’t grant me permission to collect the plants he’s bulldozing the first time I ask- I’d go right ahead and save the poor suckers before they get destroyed - permission or none! This is just my viewpoint and I actually haven’t done any collecting before but there’s a time when normal ethics meant to profit landowners need to be thrown out the window
